Certain stages from manufacturing to installation, detailed in Table 3, depend on critical raw material inputs that have their own supply chain vulnerabilities, making the process particularly sensitive to disruptions. The most critical upstream input is GOES, which forms the laminated core of the transformer. Once designs are finalized, the first physical step is the preparation of core and winding materials. Winding core assembly requires skilled labor and is one of the 8 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies at www.nlr.gov/publications. most time-consuming stages of transformer production compared to other steps such as conservator assembly. Industry interviewees noted that newer assembly equipment is more sophisticated, improving output and efficiency. GOES is processed into thin laminations that form the magnetic core while copper or aluminum conductors are drawn and shaped into forms such as foil, round wire, or CTC cables.
